props.name: items
props.description: The trail, oldest first — the last entry is the current page.  A JSON array of `{ label, href? }`. `href` is optional precisely because the last item normally has none: the current page is not a link.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the landmark. Defaults to "Breadcrumb".

ai.summary: Shows where the current page sits in a hierarchy, oldest ancestor first.
whenToUse: The page is more than two levels deep
The reader needs to move up one or more levels
The hierarchy, not the history, is what matters — this is not a back button
whenNotToUse: The page is flat or one level deep — a breadcrumb with one item says nothing
You want to go back to where the reader came from — use a Link or the browser's back
The trail is a stepped process — use a Stepper
ai.accessibility: `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` wrapping an `<ol>`, so it is a landmark a screen reader can jump to and announces as a hierarchy rather than as unrelated links. The last item carries `aria-current="page"` and is not a link — a link to the page you are on is a no-op that reads as actionable. Separators are drawn with `::before` and carry no text, so nothing announces between the items.
knownLimitations: An empty trail renders nothing at all rather than an empty landmark
`items` is JSON, not slotted children, because the component must know which entry is last
